questions.question: Increasing k smooths the decision boundary.

explanations.a: Correct. Increasing k smooths the decision boundary because predictions are averaged over more neighbours, reducing sensitivity to noise.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Larger k values do smooth decision boundaries by considering more neighbours.

questions.question: Feature scaling is optional for KNN.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Feature scaling is essential for KNN as distance calculations are strongly affected by feature magnitudes.
explanations.b: Correct. Feature scaling is not optional for KNN since distance-based calculations are strongly affected by feature magnitudes.

questions.question: The Iris dataset has three target classes.

explanations.a: Correct. The Iris dataset has three target classes: Setosa, Versicolor, and Virginica.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The Iris dataset does have exactly three species classes.

questions.question: KNN always builds a parameterized model.

explanations.a: Incorrect. KNN is a non-parametric, instance-based algorithm that does not build an explicit model.
explanations.b: Correct. KNN does not build a parameterized model because it stores training data and classifies samples directly at prediction time.

questions.question: ROC-AUC can be computed for multi-class KNN classification.

explanations.a: Correct. ROC-AUC can be computed for multi-class KNN using one-vs-rest or one-vs-one evaluation strategies.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Multi-class ROC-AUC computation is possible using appropriate strategies.

questions.question: Stratified sampling helps maintain class proportions.

explanations.a: Correct. Stratified sampling maintains class proportions by ensuring each class is equally represented in training and testing sets.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Stratified sampling is specifically designed to preserve class distribution.

questions.question: Euclidean distance is sensitive to feature scaling.

explanations.a: Correct. Euclidean distance is sensitive to feature scaling because features with larger ranges dominate distance calculations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Distance metrics like Euclidean distance are strongly influenced by feature magnitudes.

questions.question: KNN performs well on very high-dimensional data without issues.

explanations.a: Incorrect. KNN suffers from the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional spaces.
explanations.b: Correct. KNN does not perform well in high-dimensional spaces due to the curse of dimensionality reducing distance reliability.

questions.question: Iris dataset is originally published in 1936.

explanations.a: Correct. The Iris dataset was published in 1936 by Ronald A. Fisher in his study on discriminant analysis.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Fisher published the Iris dataset in 1936.

questions.question: Confusion matrix shows prediction errors by class.

explanations.a: Correct. A confusion matrix shows prediction errors by class by comparing actual labels with predicted labels.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Confusion matrices are specifically designed to show classification performance across classes.
